name: CPTS Exam Methodology & Playbook
command: # Loop: Recon -> Initial Access -> Pillage -> PrivEsc -> Loot -> AD -> Lateral -> Pivot -> (repeat) -> Report
description: Start-to-finish orientation for the CPTS exam (multi-host internal pentest + report). The phase loop, which card to reach for at each step, the 'when stuck' checklist, and the time-wasting mistakes to avoid. Open this when you land on a new host or get stuck.

steps.label: 1. New network/host -> RECON (do not jump to exploit)
steps.command: # Conservative nmap first (full TCP -p-, then -sCV on open), then UDP top ports. Web: whatweb/gobuster/ffuf, check robots.txt + vhosts. Identify services & roles before touching anything. Cards: nmap-*, ffuf-web-fuzz, gobuster, gs-web-recon.

steps.label: 2. Initial access
steps.command: # Default/weak creds first, then service misconfig, web attacks (SQLi/LFI/upload/cmdi), then public exploits (searchsploit) LAST. Cards: default creds, sqlmap-*, lfi-*, file-upload-*, cmdi-*, exploit-vetting.

steps.label: 3. Low-priv shell -> PILLAGE before privesc
steps.command: # Stabilise TTY, then hunt creds/configs/history/db strings and TEST them everywhere (reuse!). Only then escalate. Cards: spawn-tty/tty-shell-upgrade, linux-cred-hunt, findstr-hunt, win-file-search-ps, snaffler, lazagne-run.

steps.label: 4. Local privilege escalation
steps.command: # Run enum (linPEAS/winPEAS, linux-enum-*, winpe-*), then the specific vector. Cards: winpe-initial-enum, linux-enum-*, seimpersonate-printspoofer, weak-service-binary, sudo/cron/SUID (linux), missing-patch-enum.

steps.label: 5. Priv esc achieved -> LOOT EVERYTHING
steps.command: # Dump creds/hashes/tickets, SSH keys, browser/DPAPI, KeePass. Re-run AD enum with the new context. Cards: mimikatz-lsadump, secretsdump-*, lsass-dump, mimikatz-dpapi-chrome, ntds-vss.

steps.label: 6. Active Directory
steps.command: # Enumerate (BloodHound + ldapdomaindump), then attack: SYSVOL/GPP passwords, Kerberoast, AS-REP roast, ACL abuse, delegation, DCSync, trusts. Cards: ad-bloodhound-python, ad-ldapdomaindump, ad-gpp-*, ad-kerberoast*, ad-asrep*, ad-acl-*, ad-*-delegation, ad-*-dcsync, ad-trust*.

steps.label: 7. Lateral movement
steps.command: # Reuse creds/hashes/tickets across hosts. Cards: pth-* (PtH), *-ptt (PtT), impacket-exec (psexec/wmiexec/smbexec/atexec), evil-winrm, crackmapexec/netexec, mssql lateral.

steps.label: 8. New pivot -> RE-SCAN from the new position (never skip)
steps.command: # Set up the tunnel, then re-enumerate the newly reachable subnet from scratch. Cards: ligolo-ng-pivot, chisel-socks, ssh-dynamic-socks, sshuttle, msf-autoroute. Then loop back to step 1 for the new network.

steps.label: 9. Documentation & report (continuous)
steps.command: # Screenshot every finding (command + output + host) AS YOU GO. Track hosts/creds/findings. Cards: report-components, pentest-lifecycle.

examples.label: When stuck: always check SYSVOL for GPP passwords
examples.command: # mount \\<dc>\SYSVOL ; grep -r cpassword ; or ad-gpp-* card

notes: PHASE LOOP (from EXAM FLOW): new host -> recon -> initial access -> pillage -> privesc -> loot -> AD -> lateral -> pivot -> RE-SCAN -> repeat -> report. WHEN STUCK: re-read the recon results, re-test creds EVERYWHERE (assume reuse), check SYSVOL/GPP, re-enumerate. TIME-WASTING MISTAKES TO AVOID (from DO-NOT-REPEAT): (1) Don't ignore SYSVOL - check GPP cpassword early. (2) ALWAYS test credential reuse across hosts/services. (3) Don't overfocus on CVEs - misconfig/creds/privesc win more boxes. (4) RE-ENUMERATE after every pivot - the new subnet is fresh attack surface. (5) Scan FROM the new network position after pivoting. (6) Don't skip 'too basic' things (robots.txt, default creds). (7) Don't overtrust nmap -O; read service banners. (8) Treat 'filtered' as a firewall signal, not 'service absent' - validate with -sA ACK scan, --source-port, or an internal pivot before ruling out AD. (9) Don't over-tune nmap speed (-T5/low retries) on discovery - you silently miss hosts/services; go conservative first, speed up only after confirming visibility. (10) Business-critical data services often survive on non-standard ports where standard ones are filtered. LINKED CARDS: search the ids named in each step.
